x_pinakes.title: Pinakes capability manifest — the canonical resolver/producer on the Koine capability bus
x_pinakes.description: The KCB (`koine/specs/capability-bus.md` §2) manifest Pinakes publishes as the authority provider named in that spec's §6 per-project mapping. It is a SURFACE WRAPPER, not an implementation: every capability below points at code that is already built and merged (the Wikidata OpenRefine reconciler `packages/culture-scrape/src/culturescrape/schema/reconcile.py`, the csid resolver `server/services/graph-resolver.ts`, the graph query layer `server/routes/graph.ts`, and the canonical-TSV / entity-grounding exporters under `scripts/`). Nothing here re-implements a reconciler. The manifest exists so a consumer can DISCOVER those surfaces through the bus; because §3 is route-by-lookup rather than proxy, a consumer that cannot reach the Cuneiform-hosted registry can read this document from Pinakes directly (`/.well-known/kcb-manifest.json`) and invoke the same endpoints — Pinakes never depends on the registry to serve its capabilities.
x_pinakes.endpointNote: Pinakes fronts the KCB §6 capabilities as MCP tools at `endpoints.mcp` (`/mcp`, official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) and as A2A skills on the agent-card at `endpoints.a2a` (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`, official `@a2a-js/sdk`) in addition to plain HTTP (`endpoints.http`); the agent-card also carries this whole manifest as a `https://koine.dev/kcb/manifest/0.3` AgentCard extension (KCB §2). The per-capability `x_surfaces` are the already-built routes the MCP tools, the A2A skills, and the HTTP base all front; they are the direct-invocation path the §3 registry hands out addresses for.
x_pinakes.authNote: `auth.grants_required` fixes the KCB §5 grant SHAPE only. Grant issuance and spend ceilings live in Cuneiform's workforce governance; Pinakes's own HTTP surfaces keep enforcing their existing `server/services/api-auth.ts` policy until a grant issuer exists.
x_pinakes.signingNote: KCB §5 says manifests SHOULD be signed. No Ed25519 key is provisioned for Pinakes yet, so `signing.key_id` is null (unsigned) while the shape is already the one KGP `manifest.signing` uses, so signing is a key-provisioning step and not a schema change.

produces.description: The canonical node/edge TSV bundle — typed Neo4j-import headers from `shared/canonical-schema.json`, csid-keyed, with the four provenance columns on every row. Grounding-only: reference data a consumer grounds against, never runtime logic.

The entity-grounding pack (csid, entity type, aliases, reconciliation, provenance, licence classes) in the KGP `koine/specs/grounding-pack.md` §2 envelope: content-addressed `pack_id`, `worlds`/`kind`/`basis`/`dialect`, `exact_match` anchor assertions carrying §3 claim ids, and a §7.1 `license_policy` manifest. Contract: `docs/grounding-pack.md`.

Canonical real-world entity references (csids). KINP §6 names Pinakes the single canonical authority for real-world entities, so this port is the one every other project's `same_as` anchors point at. The list is total over `shared/canonical-schema.json` nodeTypes and is drift-checked by `assertValidCapabilityManifest`.

consumes.description: Grounding-only knowledge from peer producers (Analyzer extraction deltas, Insimul world facts downshifted for export). Arrives through the contribution review queue, never as a live write — KCB §5 merge-review linkage.
Entity references to resolve or reconcile, in any canonical type.

capabilities.name: resolve
capabilities.description: Resolve a Pinakes entity reference (canonical node type + local `pinakes_id`, or a name) to its canonical `cs:<type>:<local>` csid — the KINP entity CURIE per `docs/canonical-schema.md` §3.1. Exact alias hits resolve at confidence 1.0; a tie between distinct csids returns no match rather than guessing.

x_surfaces.description: Entity ref → csid, with the resolution method and confidence.
Permanent entity id → canonical descriptor + canonical URL.

capabilities.name: reconcile
capabilities.description: Reconcile a name-anchored row against Wikidata through the OpenRefine-style reconciliation API and, on a confident match, stamp the QID and re-mint the csid as QID-anchored — which is what collapses two sources onto one identity. KINP §6.1 makes Wikidata the primary real-world anchor; this is the resolver authority behind it.

x_surfaces.description: Runs the Wikidata acquisition + reconciliation pipeline for one domain; every matched/ambiguous/none decision is recorded in the row's provenance and lands in the contribution review queue.
The reconcilable domains + their Wikidata classes (the input vocabulary for the POST above).

capabilities.name: query
capabilities.description: Query the canonical graph corpus — Datalog over the constrained-Horn projection, Cypher over Neo4j, lexical search, and GraphRAG neighborhood retrieval. Answers are grounding-only: facts about consensus reality, not evaluable runtime logic.

x_surfaces.description: Read-only Cypher against the Neo4j projection.
Lexical search over the graph corpus.
